source.citation: Unidentified author, article on nervous and reflex cough, Medical Record 56 (August 5, 1899): 189. Author and title to confirm from the page image.

complaints: three months of a strange cough about once a minute, like the bleating of a sheep
presentation.course: Seen February 10, 1897, after three months of the cough. Referred by her physician, whose treatment had failed.
presentation.priorTreatment: Unspecified treatment by the referring physician, without effect.

findings: glottis almost closed during a paroxysm (laryngoscope), from spasm rather than paralysis
little control by will; never occurs during sleep
outcome: The cough faded gradually after a year and a half; other hysterical signs remained.
quotes: It sounded more like the bleating of a sheep than any- thing else
the cough never occurred during sleep

modernReading.text: Functional (psychogenic or habit) cough, or possibly a vocal tic. It stops in sleep and has no lung cause; it usually settles with time and calm handling.

fixed: repetitive odd cough without chest disease

constrained.rule: a parent usually tells the history

free: what the family fears it is

notes: The doctor needs a throat or chest examination to rule out disease. Fear of consumption would be a natural worry for the family.
